purpose: Robustness battery for control C0 (no new strategy variant). Questions: does C0's entry selection beat random entries with the same exits; how bad can drawdowns plausibly get; is the result concentrated in one year or regime; does it sit on a parameter plateau; does it survive harsher execution, a survivorship haircut and a benchmark comparison. C0 itself is never changed by this file.
execution_model: strategy.research_config(): realistic costs, 10 bps slippage, 5% volume and 2% ADV caps (as PREREG_v1/v2), plus two accounting corrections: risk per share and the R unit are measured from the planned buy-stop to the stop (the live screener's sizing), and entries are sized on equity known before the entry session. Design-window numbers are computed on data truncated at design_end so no design trade uses 2025+ prices. Stress scenarios are applied on top.

windows.holdout_rule: Everything except test R-HO uses the design window only. R-HO opens the 2025+ window once for C0, logged in experiments/holdout_log.jsonl; a second opening under this hash is refused.
windows.contamination_note: 2025+ is also the hold-out of PREREG_v1 and v2, so it has been looked at for other hypotheses. R-HO therefore counts as a confirmation, not a fresh test.

multiple_testing.family: PREREG_v1 H1-H8 (8) + benchmarks.md H2,H3 (2) + V2-1..V2-3 (3) + the 12-variant exit/entry grid C0 was selected from (12) + R-NULL-A, R-NULL-B, R-CI, R-BENCH (4)
multiple_testing.note: Only the four inferential tests carry an alpha. The 12 grid trials are counted because C0 was selected from them (selection bias); counting them does not remove the in-sample selection effect, which stays a stated limit.

inferential_tests.name: C0 versus random entries (any bar)
inferential_tests.method: For every signal date, draw as many random (symbol, date) entries as C0 took on that date, from bars of the universe that C0 did NOT signal and whose buy-stop would trigger. Same entry rule, stop, exit, hold limit and realistic costs. Statistic: mean net R per trade. 2000 draws, seed 20261015. One-sided p = (1 + draws with mean >= C0) / (1 + draws).
inferential_tests.note: Pool A includes non-uptrend bars where a breakout buy-stop does worse, so A is easy to pass. R-NULL-B is the informative one; the verdict needs both.

inferential_tests.name: C0 versus random stage-2 entries
inferential_tests.method: As R-NULL-A, but the pool is restricted to bars that pass C0's stage-2 and filter rules but fall below the score threshold or have no setup. Isolates what the Supertrend/setup/score layer adds on top of the trend filter.

inferential_tests.name: C0 expectancy is positive
inferential_tests.method: Quarter-clustered bootstrap CI (2000 resamples, seed 0) of the mean net R per trade, at confidence 1 - alpha_per_test. Quarters, not months, because positions are held for months and adjacent months overlap.

inferential_tests.name: C0 beats exposure-matched Nifty
inferential_tests.method: Paired daily net return of C0 minus the Nifty held at C0's average invested fraction (rest in cash at 0%). The Nifty price index excludes dividends that the adjusted stock series include, so an assumed 1.3%/yr dividend yield is added back. No beta adjustment is made (the traded universe is higher-beta than the Nifty), which still favours C0 slightly. Quarter-clustered bootstrap CI of the mean at alpha_per_test.

tolerance_gates.name: Monte Carlo drawdown tolerance
tolerance_gates.method: Stationary block bootstrap (mean block 63 trading days, 5000 paths, seed 20261015) of C0's design-window daily net portfolio returns; path length equals the design window. A second set of paths as short as the hold-out is used for R-HO.
tolerance_gates.pass: 95th percentile max drawdown no deeper than 35% AND probability of a max drawdown of 25% or more is at most 25%
tolerance_gates.note: These are risk tolerances chosen before results, not statistical claims. They can be tightened by the user, never loosened after a run.

tolerance_gates.name: Not concentrated in one year or regime
tolerance_gates.method: Calendar-year net R in the design window (years with at least 15 trades) and Nifty bull/bear split at entry.
tolerance_gates.pass: average net R > 0 in at least 60% of those years AND no single year contributes more than 40% of total net R

tolerance_gates.name: Parameter plateau
tolerance_gates.method: One-at-a-time neighbours of C0 (design window, realistic costs): min score 58/65/79/86, max hold 96/144, exit EMA span 40/60, ATR stop multiple 1.2/1.8, stop floor 2.4%/3.6%. Neighbours are descriptive; none is ever adopted.
tolerance_gates.pass: at least 75% of neighbours keep at least 70% of C0's design Calmar AND every neighbour has net CAGR > 0

tolerance_gates.name: Execution stress
tolerance_gates.method: Design-window net CAGR under: slippage x2 and x3; statutory costs x2; +25 bps extra slippage on stop exits; liquidity caps halved; 20% of entries missed at random (5 draws); the 20% of fills with the largest gap above the buy-stop missed; and a combined harsh case (slippage x2, costs x2, +25 bps stop slippage, caps halved). After-tax CAGR (20% on positive yearly net realised gains) is reported, not gated.
tolerance_gates.pass: net CAGR > 0 in every scenario AND the combined harsh case keeps at least half of the base-case CAGR

tolerance_gates.name: Survivorship haircut (synthetic sensitivity)
tolerance_gates.method: With probability q per trade (0.5%, 1%, 2%, 3%) the trade ends in a 40% gap-down loss instead of its simulated exit (8 draws each, seed 20261015). This is NOT evidence about survivorship and does not clear gate B2; it shows how much hidden delisting risk the result can absorb. A real point-in-time universe is still required. A second sensitivity subtracts a uniform average R per trade (0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30) to mimic inclusion bias (today's constituents were partly chosen because they rose); the break-even R is reported.
tolerance_gates.pass: design net CAGR > 0 at q = 1% AND with 0.10R removed from every trade; both break-evens are reported

tolerance_gates.name: Hold-out confirmation (opened once)
tolerance_gates.method: C0's realistic net portfolio over 2025-01-01 onward. The hold-out is opened only when every other test and gate has already passed (if any has failed, the verdict is already negative and the hold-out is not spent).
tolerance_gates.pass: net CAGR > 0 AND max drawdown no deeper than the 95th percentile drawdown of Monte Carlo paths as short as the hold-out

verdict_rule: robustness_passed = every inferential test and every tolerance gate passes. A failure is reported, not repaired: nothing in this file is edited after a run. Passing means only that no registered robustness test rejected C0; it does not establish a live edge, does not change any readiness weight, and does not authorise live trading.
